1:- लंका में राम जी - 111 दिन रहे।
2:- लंका में सीताजी - 435 दिन रहीं।
3:-मानस में श्लोक संख्या = 27 है।
4:- मानस में चोपाई संख्या 4608 है।
5:- मानस में दोहा संख्या - 1074 है।
6:- मानस में सोरठा संख्या - 207 है।
7:-मानस में छन्द संख्या = 86 है।
8:- सुग्रीव में बल था - 10000 हाथियों का।
9:- सीता रानी बनीं 33 वर्ष की उम्र में।
10:-मानस रचना के समय तुलसीदास की उम्र 17 वर्ष थी।
11:-पुष्पक विमान की चाल 400 मील/घण्टा थी।
12:-रामादल व रावण दल का युद्ध = 87 दिन चला।
13:-राम रावण युद्ध = 32 दिन चला।
14:-सेतु निर्माण = 5 दिन में हुआ।
15:-नलनील के पिता - विश्वकर्मा जी हैं।
16:-त्रिजटा के पिता = विभीषण हैं।
17:-विश्वामित्र राम को ले गए 10 दिन के लिए।
18:-राम ने रावण को सबसे पहले मारा था 6 वर्ष की उम्र में।
19:-रावण को जिन्दा किया सुखेन बेद ने नाभि में अमृत रखकर।

श्री राम के दादा परदादा का नाम क्या था? नहीं तो जानिये-

1- ब्रह्मा जी से मरीचि हुए,
2- मरीचि के पुत्र कश्यप हुए,
3- कश्यप के पुत्र विवस्वान थे,
4-विवस्वान के वैवस्वत मनु हुए. वैवस्वत मनु के समय जल प्रलय हुआ था,
5- वैवस्वतमनु के दस पुत्रों में से एक का नाम इक्ष्वाकु था,इक्ष्वाकु ने अयोध्या को अपनी राजधानी बनाया और इस प्रकार इक्ष्वाकु कुलकी स्थापना की।
6 - इक्ष्वाकु के पुत्र कुक्षि हुए,
7- कुक्षि के पुत्र का नाम विकुक्षि था,
8 - विकुक्षि के पुत्र बाण हुए,
9 - बाण के पुत्र अनरण्य हुए,
10- अनरण्य से पृथु हुए,
11- पृथु से त्रिशंकु का जन्म हुआ,
12- त्रिशंकु के पुत्र धुंधुमार हुए,
13- धुन्धुमार के पुत्र का नाम युवनाश्व था,
14- युवनाश्व के पुत्र मान्धाता हुए,
15- मान्धाता से सुसन्धि का जन्म हुआ,
16- सुसन्धि के दो पुत्र हुए- ध्रुवसन्धि एवं प्रसेनजित,
17- ध्रुवसन्धि के पुत्र भरत हुए,
18- भरत के पुत्र असित हुए,
19- असित के पुत्र सगर हुए,
20- सगर के पुत्र का नाम असमंज था,
21- असमंज के पुत्र अंशुमान हुए,
22- अंशुमान के पुत्र दिलीप हुए,
23- दिलीप के पुत्र भगीरथ हुए, भागीरथ ने ही गंगा को पृथ्वी पर उतारा था. भागीरथ के पुत्र ककुत्स्थ थे।
24- ककुत्स्थ के पुत्र रघु हुए, रघु के अत्यंत तेजस्वी और पराक्रमी नरेश होने के कारण उनके बाद इस वंश का नाम रघुवंश हो गया, तब से श्री राम के कुल को रघु कुल भी कहा जाता है।
25- रघु के पुत्र प्रवृद्ध हुए,
26- प्रवृद्ध के पुत्र शंखण थे,
27- शंखण के पुत्र सुदर्शन हुए,
28- सुदर्शन के पुत्र का नाम अग्निवर्ण था,
29- अग्निवर्ण के पुत्र शीघ्रग हुए,
30- शीघ्रग के पुत्र मरु हुए,
31- मरु के पुत्र प्रशुश्रुक थे,
32- प्रशुश्रुक के पुत्र अम्बरीष हुए,
33- अम्बरीष के पुत्र का नाम नहुष था,
34- नहुष के पुत्र ययाति हुए,
35- ययाति के पुत्र नाभाग हुए,
36- नाभाग के पुत्र का नाम अज था,
37- अज के पुत्र दशरथ हुए,
38- दशरथ के चार पुत्र राम, भरत, लक्ष्मण तथा शत्रुघ्न हुए।

While the Samsung S24 Ultra may present itself as a tempting pinnacle of smartphone technology, proclaiming 'why buy anything else?' overlooks a critical aspect: the underlying security and integrity of its operating system. Android, despite its advancements, still grapples with a fundamental flaw - fragmentation. This isn't just about varying experiences across devices; it's about a security model that's stretched thin over a myriad of hardware configurations and manufacturers. This fragmentation leads to inconsistent security updates and patch deployments, making Android a more inviting target for cyber threats compared to its counterpart.

In contrast, Apple's iOS, running on a tightly integrated hardware-software ecosystem, offers a more fortified front. This isn’t mere brand loyalty speaking; it's a recognition of a cohesive, controlled environment where security updates are swift and universal, reducing windows of vulnerability. The saying 'jack of all trades, master of none' aptly describes Android in this scenario – versatile, yes, but at the cost of being a master in security and integration, a domain where iOS undeniably reigns.

So, while the S24 Ultra might dazzle with its features, those serious about cybersecurity would likely question the wisdom of opting for a platform where security can be as fragmented as the devices it runs on. In the realm of digital security, it’s not just about having the flashiest tool; it's about having the most secure one. And in that arena, iOS continues to stand as the bride in a room full of bridesmaids.

But the fact that Google collaborates with Samsung to bring new features to Galaxy devices before Pixels, shows the reality that Google never expects Pixels to be mainstream phones. I'm okay with that. As long as they keep making Pixel phones and keep making them great.

Perfect review - in most other first looks and reviews I have seen - the consensus (as in this review) is that this is a solid. dependable top notch smart phone that does all the things it should do really really well. BUT the criticism universally is that it is "BORING" and not much different to its predecessor.

Well imho, smart phones are now like refrigerators - essential tools in our daily lives. I for one do NOT want "excitement" in my device. I want dependability, durability, functionality and a long usage period to offset that expensive initial cost.

Unlike reviewers and well healed "enthusiasts" I keep my phones right up until the software updates stop. Which in my case is the Note 10+ which is now 4.5 years old and is still serving me extremely well.

If the S24U is anything like the Note in the areas of dependability, durability and functionality then the 7 years of usage that I anticipate will provide the best ROI of any other Android phone.

There is no other Android phone that offers this kind of package. So yeah, more of the same is what myself and a lot of others really want.

Brilliant review, well done.

Sure, it's natural for human beings to be concerned about our image but I feel providing our worst tendencies such technology only gives them  fuel to worsen. Humans have a tendency to kill other humans; modern weaponry has only made that ability easier — allowing us to kill in the millions instead of mere thousands. Was the firearm worth it? Either way, that Pandora's box is long opened. It's too late.

Tech innovation merely for tech innovation's sake is "cool" in the moment but upon reflection is a rather foolish affair as to be so blindly in want of circumspection. Everything we do, every action we take, every economic decision has its consequence, for better or worse, that ripple through the generations of both man and animal, person and place.

text:
After using the Note 20 Ultra for 3 and a half years, I pre-ordered the S24 Ultra, 1 TB version. My Note 20 Ultra has 512 GB of storage expanded by a 256 GB SD card. I hate to lose the SD slot but the 1 TB makes up for it. The Note's cameras were good for 2020 but I can see a huge difference in my son's S23 Ultra's photos versus mine.

AT&T basically lied to me when they offered a free S21 FE with activation of a new line. After viewing my bills a couple of months later, I saw I was being charged $10 per month for it. If I were to pay $10 a month for a phone, it wouldn't be the S21 FE. I was impressed with the features of the Onelplus 12 so I opted to pre-order it as well. I'll transfer the Sim card from the S21 FE to the Oneplus 12 and use the S21 FE as a Bluetooth player for my music systems. This will give me an opportunity to compare two different flagship phones to decide which one I'd like better. It's always good to have another phone handy if my main phone has a problem. I will use the S24 Ultra as my primary phone. The best of both worlds as I see it and life is short, so why not. By the way, I'm retired and just enjoying my life nowadays.

text:
I wish influencers didn't have such a crazed love of flat screens. I'm aware of the benefits that come of them, and the trade-offs, but when it comes to an aesthetic viewpoint, I much MUCH prefer the curved screens. I also prefer swiping gestures on curved screens, especially when they have gentle curves from top to bottom.

I think my favorite looking screen, not best functioning, but based only on looks, was the extremely curved Huawei Mate 3 Pro(?) The way the screen basically wrapped 90 degrees around the sides and went considerably far down, it was just so gorgeous. 

That said, my favorite functioning curved phones are the ones that have a moderate curve on all sides. It makes the screen appear like it's a layer of water bursting at the seems of its container, while also providing the very smooth and comfortable benefit of feeling great for swiping gestures. 

Of course, to each their own. I do remember a time when everyone loved curved screens, even influencers. Now that influencers DON'T like them, no one does. 

Tick-Tock, I guess.

text:
I'll be honest. As an s24 ultra owner that upgraded from an s22 ultra (exynos). If you have an s22/s23 ultra .. there is absolutely no reason to upgrade. I upgraded because I do that every 2 years and this time my mom's phone broke down (my old s20 ultra) so I got the s24 ultra so I can also give my s22 ultra to my mom. 

Don't get me wrong, the s24 ultra so far is *incredible* .. it's also probably the smallest phone upgrade I've ever had in my life. 
Upgrades are as follows 

1. Chipset. Bro, after using this snapdragon device I'm even more angry that we got scammed with exynos for over a decade. My s22 ultra has a 120hz screen. It never, EVER felt smooth like 120 should be. Using the s24 ultra with snapdragon, it is a whole other smoothness. For the first time the screen and scrolling truly feels 120. It's how I imagined android phones would be 8 years ago, and many android phones achieved that because most flagships use snapdragon chips. But samsung never truly did in Europe because their snapdragon chips, even when they are close to snapdragon in performance aren't as consistent. They don't get the same support from devs. They seem to have harder time handling stuff long term and more likely to develop microstutters etc.

For years I was stuck getting exynos phones because I cannot do without my spen lol .. 

2. Better pictures despite having a very similar camera setup. I think also partially because of snapdragon's better picture processing. 

But that's kinda it .. the design is nearly identical. The software is basically identical. The AI features will come to older phones. The hardware is almost even a downgrade at some places (the 5x instead of 10x) 

If you're upgrading from the s20/21 and prior.. you'll have a massive upgrade. If you're upgrading from an s22/23 .. esp if that phone is snapdragon already. There is very little here to upgrade too. If you're switching from an iphone or some other brand of android phone and you're just looking for the best android phone on the market. Yeah, Marques is right, there is zero reason to get any other phone that this (if the price isn't a big factor e.g. if you're getting it with a phone contract like most people do). Samsung's phones are generally just the best android phones on the market, and their software support has gotten insanely good. They went from the bloatware company to having a better experience than stock android. 

That said, if I didn't care about an spen etc I might have picked google pixel or something instead because I live in Europe and fk exynos.

text:
First time I disliked a MKBHD video.

He is someone that criticized many times the phone manufacturers for not giving us really improvements and new features with every new model and now he makes a video (that looked more like a paid review) where he basically says Samsung S24 Ultra is the best smartphone available and you shouldn't even consider any other options. 

In my opinion, if I'm going to pay over 1300usd for a smartphone I want the best software and the best hardware. 

Don't get me wrong, OneUI is a very polished android experience, with lots of features but if you look at other android models, like Vivo X100 Pro (which, arguably, has a better main camera and ultra wide for photography than Samsung) you will notice the camera sensors, battery size, charging speed are some of the best on the market...

On the other hand, Samsung keeps using the same 5000mAh battery for the 3rd year in a row, the charging speed is limited to 45watt with cable or 25watt by wireless charging (OnePlus 12 is laughing 😂). 

The camera sensors are small (in quality and size) compared to the ones you can find in a Vivo X100 Pro, Oppo Find X7 Ultra, OnePlus 12... 

The titanium frame is just pure marketing because it doesn't improve the resistance of the smartphone to drops. Titanium has less elasticity than aluminum. For that reason, when you drop your titanium frame smartphone there is a bigger possibility the glass of the screen and back gets damaged.

Samsung has been improving a lot, at least with the last 3 models, but they also could offer much more for the price you are paying...

text:
Thank you for the video. As a power user living in The Netherlands, I'd like to share my perspective. My phone journey includes the Samsung S5 Active, S7 Edge, and currently the Oppo Find X2 Pro, which I've used for nearly 4 years. I've just preordered the OnePlus 12, as I was in the market for a new 4-year power user phone, but found it challenging to find one that meets all my criteria.

My Requirements and Wishes:

Screen Quality:
- Essential for reading, video, multitasking; looking for at least 1440p, ~500 ppi, 120Hz, AMOLED.
- Must have an excellent low light mode due to my light sensitivity.
- Prefer a folding phone with a near 9-inch screen or a non-foldable with an additional screen near/below the cameras for selfies/group video.
- Under-display or corner selfie camera, particularly for only video calls (also fine with complete removal, finger print reader is enough and back camera can be used for face unlock)
- Slight curve to the screen, no bezels (not a fan of flat or overly curved displays).

Build and Durability:
- Back body in vegan leather or marble, aluminum edges, ideally IP68 rated, shock-resistant/absorbent (I tend to drop my phone frequently).
- Titanium doesn't appeal to me in phones, though I see its value in medical devices or wearables.

Battery Life and Storage:
- Top-tier battery experience with fast charging (about half in 15 minutes), less emphasis on wireless charging.
- Long battery life on heavy usage (>7h) and extended life in power-saving mode for essential tasks.
- Minimum of 512GB ROM as I regularly use 350-450GB between yearly backups.

Performance and RAM:
- At least 12GB of RAM, ideally closer to 40GB for intensive tasks like data analytics, running open-source AI models, managing 100+ browser tabs, and using 18+ apps simultaneously.

Operating System:
- Prefer an OS that's as barebones as possible, with easy transferability of my apps and launcher (like Action Launcher), and full customization freedom.

General Preferences:
- Dark mode on everything, advanced haptic feedback, silent mode usage (due to sound sensitivity and some synesthesia).

Connectivity and Sensors:
- Complete and advanced options (Bluetooth 5.3, NFC, WiFi 6-7, 4-5G, USB-C for 4K screen or VR/AR connections), broad audio support, and comprehensive navigation technologies.

Camera Quality:
- Good to great overall performance, especially in auto or preset modes for different scenarios.

text:
Well, i got my shiny new s24 ultra 2 days ago .. . the phone is phenomenal - and is replacing my temporary iphone 12 that i had borrowed from my sister (her old phone) -- or to be more specific, it succeeds my old Note 20 Ultra.

So let me compare my old Note 20 ultra to the new s24 ultra .. hmm:
- the screen is better on the s24 .. nicer to work with, looks a little sharper (but really .. only a tiny bit. In daily usage, you wont see a difference, especially because i usually run my phone in 1080 and not QHD) - it is brighter though .. which is irrelevant in my country because we do not get bright sunlight.
- it is faster .. yes . significantly faster ... do 1-2 seconds matter in daily usage? no
- its battery lasts longer? .. no, no it does not. I have no idea what all those 12 hours screen-on-time tests do .. but neither my Note 20, nor my new s24 are noticably different in daily usage when it comes to the battery.
- the material feels better. Yes, yes it does - no beating around the bush, the new frame material and shape does feel better than the old Note 20 ultra
- AI features ... i dont care
- S-pen responsiveness - no noticable difference. Its Wacom tech .. its always perfect.
- no micro-SD on the s-series... bummer! I had my note with nearly 2 TB. the s24 ultra maxes out at 1 TB - and i am SURE .. Samsung could have squeezed a sd-card slot in there


do i regret my purchase? not at all. For me .. the 7 years updates was what i wanted. 7 years updates is environmentally friendly much more than going cardboard in phone boxes.
The new phone is a good upgrade for the Note 20 ultra (and not exactly much more expensive when you factor in inflation)

What i AM disappointed with is the colour.

I have the orange one .. that turned out to be a lot less orange and a lot more flesh colour. That went so far that i questioned my eyesight. What is WRONG with big corporations and their colours?!
The green looks grey, the grey looks grey, the blue looks grey .. the supposedly bright orange looks flesh colour, the black looks grey. Has Samsung forgotten what real colours are?

text:
Why is everyone saying that x10 zoom is better in s24 Ultra than in 23 Ultra? The photos themselves may be slightly sharper, but the most important thing is the focal length, which the s24 DOES NOT OFFER. The x10 optical zoom allows for greater creative use of the zoom, not just magnification - you can take many more such photos (if you know how) than regular close-ups.

A simple example: you are on a hike - a beautiful observation deck with an amazing view, mountains and a castle a few miles away. You want to take a photo of your partner with this beautiful view of the mountains and, most importantly: the castle. You line up and take a photo with your actual 200mp lens. The photo is of excellent quality, except that the mountains are a bit small and the castle is the size of a pinhead. You move away to the appropriate distance and take the same frame with x10 zoom. Your partner is the same size, only the castle and mountains in the background that you wanted to capture are now 10x larger.

What can I say? A great video with all the right reasons and features to buy  an S24 ultra, so I placed my preorder.
But, my Galaxy note 10+ is still great too. I then considered what my galaxy note 10+ had to offer, did a feature comparison and cancelled my preorder. 
The S24 is all that you say, but all those me features and power were not enough to change over from my "ahead of its time" Note 10+. I have the same screen size, almost the same screen pixel count, bezels almost as slim as the S24, the Note 10+ is lighter, thinner and not being a social media fanatic, I don't need all the new camera features. No for they are great for those that use them 😁
The AI features are wonderful, but I can use chat gpt on my phone or edit my photos with less capability but still good enough for my use.
Using Samsung's Bixby vision provides almost the same ability as circle to search.😊
I have no doubt this is a GREAT phone, but not enough to part with many dollars, the Note 10+ was then (2019) and still is a BRILLIANT phone. Maybe the S25? Thanks again for the great video I'm sure you'll convince prospective buyers.

text:
Here are some key takeaways from the Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra review:

1. The S24 Ultra has an excellent 6.8" 1440p, 2600 nit display with slim bezels, flat screen, anti-reflective coating, and 120Hz refresh rate. It's one of the best displays available.

2. With a 5000mAh battery, 45W charging, and optimizations, the S24 Ultra has great battery life - easily lasting a full day and sometimes two.

3. The Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 chip provides top-tier performance for gaming and multitasking. The vapor chamber cooling allows sustained performance. 

4. The quad camera system can handle any shooting scenario - wide shots, portraits, 100x zoom astro-photography, etc. New 5x telephoto camera improves zoom quality.

5. Lots of AI-powered software for editing photos, screen searching, translations, etc. Good integration with Google for features like Circle to Search.

6. Promised 7 years of security updates and major Android versions. Software support is now a strength.

7. Competitive with iPhones, with similar titanium design, camera specs, always on display, etc. Pushing each other to improve.

8. At $1300 it's very expensive, but delivers on that promise. The S24 Plus gives 90% of experience for $300 less.

text: I really miss the 6.9" display Samsung used to give in Note 20 Ultra. But now from S21 Ultra the display size is decreased down to 6.8". A phone of this caliber deserves even bigger display for fluid note taking and more immersive video viewing. Samsung also removed the very aesthetically leasing curved AMOLED display. Samsung also stuck to only 120 Hz refresh rate whereas other brands give upto 165 Hz. Oneplus has given 6.82" display in the latest Oneplus 12 series. Infinix gave 6.95" and Black Shark already gave a 7.1" display , Honor also delivered 7.12" display back in Honor 8X max. But Samsung still sticks with the relatively SMALLER 6.8" display. I don't think it is good. Personal opinions might differ but according to me Samsung ruined itself quite a lot over the past few generations in many areas. Even in case of chipset also , the previous 8 Gen 2 for galaxy had overclocked core but no underclocked but this time underclocked cores are used and Antutu score is also not good enough at all. Whereas other phoned using normal 8 Gen 3 got 2.3 Mn+ , S24 Ultra got less than 2 Mn. Whereas some other flagships got 24 GB Ram , Samsung still sticks to the prehistoric 12 GB Ram which is worthless as hell in 2024 when 24 Gb becomes a norm in flagship. What to say ? Samsung now-a-days releases underpowered phones in the name of Ultra , truly hateful , detestable , not respectable upgrade at all. Even battery size is also kept the same in Ultra but increased a bit in other two variant. Whereas Redmagic went upto 6500 mAh from 6000 mah , Oneplus , IQOO went upto 5400 mAh from 5000 mAh ,samsung still gives that damn 5000 mAh , not even 6000. But Samsung used to give 7000 mah once. The charging t=is till 45W whereas other brands long ago overtaken the 100W boundary. This is really shocking & demoralizing. AI is common in 2024 but Samsung phones is way lower than what is to be expected but in case of pricing way higher than to be expected. As a Samsung mid-range phone user myself I have to say ,Samsung flagships are the most worthless flagships in 2024.

One significant aspect that sets the iPhone apart from Android is its software. Samsung, however, has made commendable strides in this area. Nonetheless, Apple stands out by not only delivering an exceptional user interface but also by making tasks more seamless and enjoyable. Take, for instance, the Notes app—an exemplary PDF reader that comes standard with iPhones. In contrast, on Android, acquiring a similar feature often requires an additional payment. This highlights Apple's commitment to enhancing user experience by providing premium subscriptions for essential software, thereby elevating the overall functionality of their devices.

In my opinion, Android, represented by Google and Samsung, should consider a strategic shift. While maintaining their superior hardware standards, they could potentially enhance their software offerings. A compelling approach could involve a slight increase in device prices, offset by the inclusion of premium features—emulating Apple's successful model. This strategy not only aligns with consumer expectations for a seamless and enriched user experience but also positions Android as a more competitive alternative in the smartphone market.

Ultimately, this is why I believe Apple currently holds an edge. It would be intriguing to witness Samsung and Google adopt a similar strategy, leveraging their exceptional hardware capabilities and refining their software offerings to create a more compelling and unified user experience.

text:
you asked "why would you get another phone" - specifically regarding android slab phones.  I would get a sony xperia 1 v instead because it DOES NOT have the stupid hole-punch camera (nor does it have a stupid notch) - there is ZERO reason I can think of to remove display for the front facing camera when you can put it ABOVE the display (you know, where it's been for a really long time before apple decided to put notches on everything).  the sony has front facing stereo speakers that actually sound good, a camera that's pretty good (honestly any flagship phone has a nice camera these days), it's got a headphone jack with a great dac and a decent adc (so if you wanted to wire in a microphone for high quality low latency production, that's an option).  it's got a dedicated camera shutter button with half-press (which is super useful), a display resolution, brightness, and contrast that's pretty fantastic.  Further, sony's phones are factory unlocked (samsung locks everything down), so you can root it do do with it whatever you like, which also means that when it goes out of support, you can root it and install third party upgraded roms on it if you want so you can use it for a longer period of time.  The only thing that I wish were different about the xperia 1 v are 1. I wish that sony's first-party os support were longer, 2. I wish the display were 16:9 (media is 16:9 and I hate that I get black bars, also phones today are way too skinny imo), 3. I wish the headphone amp were a bit more powerful to drive high impedance audiophile headphones (I still need an external amp for my nice cans)

tl;dr: I wish phones would stop eating into the display with their front camera, put it at the top.  give me good front facing stereo speakers, a great dac/headphone amp, give me back 16:9 aspect ratio phones so I can enjoy full screen media.  if they re-released a slightly larger version of the nexus 6p with a modern soc, upgraded display, and more ram, I'd buy it tomorrow.

text:
Coming from an iPhone/Mac user... S24 Ultra actually looks/sounds pretty great. Two issues I noticed (based on this video): One, it doesn't have the ecosystem. Texting/calling from your computer is cool. Google kind of offers this, and Microsoft kind of offers this, but it's pretty half-assed. With Apple, it just works, and it works perfectly. Taking a call on a MacBook sounds ten billion percent better than speakerphone, for both parties. It's not that big a deal because Telegram (et al) is better than text and it's on desktop/tablet platforms as well, and calling is another thing we can do with apps.

The other is the actual updates... I don't doubt Samsung's commitment... to Korea. So Koreans will get those seven years of updates. Everyone else but Americans will get them sometime after, and Americans tend to get the updates last. I do like Samsung promising updates (note that Apple never has — they just do it), but they need to figure out the timing. The cool thing about Apple updates is, it doesn't matter if you're in Apple's home country, or a country Apple likes, or a country Apple doesn't like. Regardless of your country's politics, if you have an iPhone, you get your updates on that day (or later if you want). If you have a Samsung, when and if are big question marks. And I realize there are hurdles unique to the Android ecosystem that need to be overcome, but frankly, it's been over a decade, they need to figure this out.

Bonus: Android jankiness. When you have 2-3x the RAM of an iPhone, and the processor is somewhat comparable, the performance should be buttery smooth. Google has been throwing that term around for over a decade now (Project Butter, anyone), but it's... never... quite... happened. Android phones are still janky AF, and Android users deserve better. I realize you got too many cooks in the kitchen with Android (and we're gonna add one more by using Nova Launcher), but there could be something (though I'm not sure what) to smooth it out. So generally Android phones can feel faster at times, than iPhones, but then they trip over themselves and it's just kinda cheap feeling. Whereas an iPhone will feel a bit slower, but it's consistent — and then, five years later, that iPhone still has that same performance, and a year or two later, the Android phone is struggling. It still feels like a beta/Labs kind of project. With iPhone, I feel like a valued customer. With Android, I feel like a beta tester, and that's fine, but, you know... maybe comp some of the phone's price for me. Oh, and all the personal data Google collects should be worth something, too. Or maybe they should quit doing that if you're paying $1300 for a phone.

The only real big thing that's still keeping me from Samsung is the bloatware from both Samsung and the US carriers. 

In terms of the carriers, I don't know how both Google and Apple both got away with not having to put carrier bloatware in their phones but Samsung still does it. I love T-Mobile but I hate setting up a new phone only to just have countless awful apps I don't want on there, with T-Mobile messages popping up here and there about more apps and services to use. Not to mention just the carrier logo and jingles that still pop up when you start the phone up. 

Samsung's own bloatware drives me perhaps even more crazy with all of their replacements for Google apps and services. Bixby, Samsung Keyboard, Galaxy App Store, Clock, Gallery, you name it. I understand that sometimes in order to add features you may have to create your own skin, but it just goes too far most times away from what Google designs. Maybe it's getting better because it seems like the Messages app is now straight Google Messages but man, setting up a new Samsung phone for me, taking all the Samsung stuff I can off the phone and replacing it back to Google apps is really annoying and you still can't completely rid of Bixby.

yeah this doesnt fully negate the convenience of an sd card slot, but it does have its own benifits

text:
Just to warn everyone, there's only one thing that the S24 fails in, games. (read more)



You see, the chipset of high end androids usually all end up in similar performance, other than "gaming specific phones" which end up being a bit better.

However, most, if not, all of those gaming phones have a problem, they put down almost everything else. This is why at least for me, and I bet a majority usually stick with high end flagships if they can afford it.

Sadly, ever since they thinned out the phones since the S22 Ultra, thermals have taken an absolute nosedive continuing with the following generations. Unless you play simple games, your experience will be quite awful without accessories like a third party fan for your phone, and even then those don't do it justice from personal experience.

I was incredibly dissapointed when I got my S22 and tried emulating or playing something like cod mobile/genshin on high quality graphics.

The S20 Ultra had a bit of performance issues in games, but its thermals were great by my anecdotal experience, even when being brought to its knees. However, despite the S22 being better by a long shot in performance, in heavy loads, it lags behind the S20 heavily due to easy overheating.

Sadly, it was not addressed nor fized at all with the S23, and even the S24 still has big issues with thermals, being worse than any other high end flagship, even being destroyed by the pixel 8, which is not meant to be extremely powerful, and that dissapointed me.

I guess I'll continue to have to bring my bulky Steam Deck with me on even small travels to families or friends just to not have to deal with my hands sweating from the heat playing a simple Playstation 2 game on the go.

However intensive gaming and thermals were the only serious caveat for me, so if you don't do that at all, no need to worry and just get the phone.

TL;DR - Thermals are awful, big games and PS2 to Wii cant run well within tenperatures.

text:
I purchased the S24 Ultra and in general I am pretty happy with it, but I also bought the OP12 to compare... and man, after a week of using the S24 Ultra and sort of quietly half hating the boxy design, I couldn't believe what a breath of fresh air it was to hold the OP12. 

I know so many people have had bad experiences breaking their curved edge screens, and so many people are just absolutely ready to move on from curved displays... and if I'm being honest, it is far and away the corners and not the edges of the screens.

Every time I would use the S24U it would remind me of all the reasons why I preferred it over the OP12... save for battery life and charging, the S24U really does everything better (even software now that OP has lost their way)... but holy cow, every time I picked up the OP12 I would just sigh to myself about how much better it felt.

So to answer your opening question... I would buy something else because this boxy design is just terrible. If it's to make room for the SPen, then take the SPen away. Make a Note again or something for people that want that. I just want a premium "ultra" device that does it all right and isn't in an uncomfortable form factor (and I have big hands... can only imagine how people with small hands feel).

text:
Received my S24 Ultra yesterday.. it's my first non-Pixel since the Galaxy S9, and I didn't even finishing setting this thing up before I was reminded of why I stuck with Pixel for so long. The required Samsung account, and the litany of applications that are preloaded,and which I can't remove, drives me insane. Also.. having now shot some side-by-side comparison photos, while the Samsung camera is no doubt excellent, in every mode (and especially in portrait) it is far slower to actually capture a photo than my Pixel 7 pro. To the extent that when taking a simultaneous portrait of my dog I ended up with a nice photo on my Pixel, and the blurry end of a tail as he exited the frame before the Samsung finished the capture. I'll daily the S24 and hope the software improves, but only until the Pixel 9 lands. 

On a positive note...as always, the hardware/fit&finish is excellent 👌

text:
Back in 2011, I was awestruck by the Galaxy Note, both because of its size and the pen it came with. The Note / Ultra lineup will probably keep its soft spot in my heart. 

However, there are a few reasons that would probably make me sell it and buy an Xperia 1. The camera is just as good, it's narrower and thus easier to firmly hold in one hand, it has ridged sides for extra grip, a physical shutter, a micro SD slot and a 3.5 mm port. I can always buy a pen for the Xperia 1 V, but I'd never be able to expand the memory of my S24 Ultra.

Still....7 years of support speaks volumes. Samsung wouldn't take the risk of promising 7 years of support on an unreliable piece of hardware.

text:
Call me crazy but I really wish they'd  make a sleek and sexy phone with all the same bells and whistles but WITHOUT 500 hideous and bulky cameras on the back. I'm sure my personal opinion is unpopular, but not everyone deems themself a professional photographer. In fact, I actually hate taking photos/video, and literally almost never even use any of the cameras on any of my previous phones. Call me crazy, but I'd even be fine with a flagship phone that had zero cameras, and in fact might even prefer it. But realistically, I believe just one camera is appropriate, ONE. And if it's not too much to ask that it not be unseemly, and be flush with the rear of the device, or atleast as close as possible.

Also, all of these iPhone similarities ("Just like the iPhone") are actually negatives for me, not positives. I can understand competing with the iPhone, but competing shouldn't be mimicry. Such tactics may work well in captivating the interests and desires of iPhone users and fans, but for those that never even liked iPhone to begin with, it's counterproductive. One thing that I loved about Samsung in the past, and with many of my older model Samsung phones was how they were DIFFERENT from iPhone, and NOT how they were similar. I also noticed immediately how even the overall shape and design of the phone seems more "box-y" and very reminiscent of iPhone design, which was an immediate disappointment to me, as a huge fan of older Samsung phones that were sleek, beveled, and stylish.

text: THANK YOU for finally saying "Just like the iPhone". I like both eco systems and have owned both iPhone AND Samsung phones but I'm SO TIRED of everyone acting like only Samsung makes interesting things. They've literally copied EACH OTHER for years and they go BACK AND FORTH. But, I will say, this Samsung is absolutely sexy and the boxy outer shell almost made me jump eco systems. But I just love the apple ecosystem and how it handles handing off messages and airpod audio from one device to the other. Everything just... works so smoothly. But the biggest deal breaker for me, and I've been complaining about it for years, is the samsung screens. I don't know why NO ONE NOTICES, but their screen has this really WEIRD oily look to it. Like I can see the pixels and they look oily even if you don't touch the screen. and when you touch the screen it GETS WORSE. I don't know how else to explain it, the screen looks bad. I've tried to point it out to my husband and he can't see what I'm talking about, which makes it even weirder, how has NO ONE NOTICED? To add to that, the iPhone adjusts it's hue based on the lighting it's in, and while the samsung does this too, it doesn't do it nearly as well as the iphone. I was in the store having them side by side and the samsung just continued to have a cooler tone, the colors just were not represented right. On it's own, it looks great, but when you compare it to the iphone, it doesn't look nearly as good. The iphone had a warmer hue to it and it had a more natural color. I tried to manually adjust the samsung and it just refused to budge. It gets warm, but barely noticeable. Like when I had them side by side, the iphone had a paper-esque look to it, like I wasn't staring at a screen, but the samsung was painfully obvious. I just couldn't get past that. Between that and the oily pixelation of their screens, nope. It looks like... it looks like when you put a shitty screen protector on it and it fucks the screen up! That's what it looks like! And you can't remove the screen protector because that's how the screen actually is. Like... I can not stare at that, absolute deal breaker for me. Bummer.

If anyone has a solution that works, I'd be ready to switch back to Android, because the Galaxy S24 Ultra is really tempting me.

The only Android phone where I find that voice commands work right out of the box is on Google's Pixels. The problem is that I don't necessarily want a Pixel; I generally prefer Samsung, especially their high-end models.

It not only allows me to write much faster to many different people, but I am also disabled, so it's much less exhausting for me to speak than to type long texts by hand

text:
Why NOT to buy the s24 ultra:

GSM Arena:

No notification light
No SD card
No headphone jack
No fm radio
No IR blaster 
Poor display 
Low quality charging cable 
No charger
Only a 5000 mah battery with no AI assist

To our surprise and disappointment, there is a *virtual* proximity sensor - Samsung Palm Proximity Sensor V2.

The  S24 Ultra exhibited massive thermal throttling in our testing and lost a huge chunk of its maximum performance over time, a whopping 53% in 3DMark. This is notably worse than both the S24+ and the S24, as well as the S23 Ultra. While you could call this an okay showing, it's still more on the disappointing end of things.

Verdict
The Galaxy S24 Ultra surprised us - we didn't expect it to have any flaws, and suddenly, we have a cons section. With a list in it. Indeed, most perplexing is the fact that Samsung has produced a display that is anything less than perfect. Of course, it's not that bad, and its shortcomings are minuscule or will be addressed later in software. But that's not what we'd expect from Samsung's ultimate smartphone.

Cons
The display has flaws which may be obscure or fixable along the way but mar the overall impression.
Charging speed is still behind the curve; the phone is picky about adapters, and the bundled cable is 3A only.
Illogical image quality disparity between 10x and slightly lower zoom levels.

Comment by an S24 Ultra user: 

Last year I lost my regular S21. As I needed a phone, I went to the shop and got myself an S23 Ultra-a great phone with an awesome display, way over my S21. After a couple of days, the S21 was found and I returned the S23 Ultra, thinking it is not the time to invest in a new phone, as I was expecting the new Samsung generation. After having the S23 Ultra experience, I didn't think twice this year and got myself a S24 Ultra, thinking that it is as least as good as the 23. But, well, the display colors from my S21 are better than the ones from the S24 Ultra. The phone is working follweles, but I am still having a hard time adapting to the new and way inferior display.

text:
Thank you so so so much for posting a long term review unlike other reviewers who just moves on with the latest releases.
I've been an S23 Ultra user since the very first week of it's launch,it has been a wonderful experience up until almost 6 months ago I've started facing issues wih the quality of the device. Ironically right after the warranty coverage,to be precise.
1) Back glass adhesive is rubbish,just like every samsung phone with even a slightly curved back panel. The adhesive gets so weak,the glass pops open on its own,so there goes the IP rating.(This is not my first samsung phone with a poor back glass adhesive issue. My friends,relatives,every single person I know has this issue)
2) I'm not a heavy user and I only fast charge my device only if I'm in an emergency. So it's been a year and seven months now, the  battery backup has gone rubbish. I've checked with the samsung store,they said Samsung batteries are good for only 450-500 cycles. So in layman's terms,almost 1.5 years of use,one charge a day.
3) Ticking time bomb,whenit comes to updates and green line issues.(Usual stuff for smartphones these days)
Please mind the back glass adhesive issue and better avoid any water contact even if the manufacturer claims IP rating. They will not provide a warranty for water ingress.
Build quality has to improve.
Lots of love to sarath bro for doing this video and I'm sorry for the extremely long comment.

I know what you're thinking: "Another S series phone? How is this any different?" Well, let me tell you, the S24 is a game-changer, and it's all in the details.

Sure, on paper, the S23 and S24 look pretty similar. But when you hold them side-by-side, you'll feel the difference. Samsung has somehow managed to make the S24 feel smoother and more comfortable to hold, despite having almost identical dimensions. The slightly rounded edges and matte finish on the frame are a world apart from the sharp corners and glossy finish of the S23. And let's not forget that annoying paint chipping issue on the S23? Yeah, that's been fixed.

At 168 grams, it's incredibly lightweight without sacrificing durability. It's like holding a feather, but one that can handle whatever you throw at it. If you've ever tried to use a brick like the iPhone 14 Pro with its 206-gram weight, you'll appreciate the S24 even more.

So, if you're in the market for a new phone and want something that not only looks good but feels amazing in your hand, the Samsung Galaxy S24 is a no-brainer.

text:
Dear Samsung,

I am writing to express my frustration regarding the resolution of photos uploaded from my S23 Ultra and S24 Ultra series devices to social media platforms like Facebook.

Despite the impressive camera quality and large resolution of these devices, I’ve noticed a significant reduction in image quality once they are uploaded to social media. The photos appear much blurrier and lack the sharpness I see in my gallery. It’s incredibly frustrating, as it diminishes the value of having such a high-resolution camera.

In comparison, I’ve noticed that iPhone users do not face this issue, and photos remain clear even after uploading to platforms like Facebook. It would be great if you could work on optimizing the resolution for social media uploads, so users can fully enjoy the benefits of their device's camera without experiencing such quality degradation.

It would be extremely helpful if an update could be made that allows users to select the highest resolution possible for uploads to platforms like Facebook and Instagram, ensuring the images retain their quality when shared. Additionally, it would be fantastic if there were a feature that lets users select all photos in an album at once and convert them to the desired resolution, rather than having to edit each photo individually.

I hope you listen to consumer/user suggestions. I’m truly disappointed when I take great photos only for them to become blurry when uploaded to social media. With fewer users relying on Google Drive or other platforms nowadays, it would be great if your devices were more social media-friendly.

. I look forward to seeing future improvements.

text:
Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra vs. iPhone 16 Pro Max: Why the Galaxy S24 Ultra Shines Brighter

The battle between Samsung's Galaxy S24 Ultra and Apple's iPhone 16 Pro Max represents the peak of innovation from two of the most influential smartphone manufacturers. While both devices are undeniably powerful, the Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra edges out the competition with its feature-packed versatility, highlighted by the unrivaled utility of the S Pen.

Display and Design

The Galaxy S24 Ultra continues Samsung’s tradition of delivering industry-leading displays. Its 6.8-inch AMOLED 2X panel with QHD+ resolution and a refresh rate of up to 120Hz provides an unmatched visual experience. While the iPhone 16 Pro Max boasts its always-impressive Super Retina XDR display, it lacks the dynamic color vibrancy and sheer customizability that Samsung offers.

Samsung’s slightly boxier design also accommodates a larger screen-to-body ratio and integrates the S Pen without compromising ergonomics—a standout feature Apple has yet to replicate.

The S Pen Advantage

The inclusion of the S Pen in the Galaxy S24 Ultra transforms it from a typical smartphone into a productivity powerhouse. Here’s where the S Pen gives the Galaxy S24 Ultra a substantial edge:

Enhanced Productivity: The S Pen enables precise note-taking, sketching, and editing on the go. Whether you're annotating documents, creating intricate designs, or simply jotting down ideas, the S Pen offers accuracy unmatched by any stylus-less alternative. Apple's Pro Max offers no comparable tool for creatives and professionals.

Remote Control Capabilities:
The S Pen doubles as a remote for controlling presentations, snapping photos, and even navigating media apps. This added functionality makes the Galaxy S24 Ultra ideal for multitasking and content creation.

Precision in Editing:
Whether you're editing photos, videos, or documents, the S Pen’s fine tip allows unparalleled control. Paired with Samsung's One UI software enhancements, it turns the phone into a mini design studio.

Advanced Handwriting-to-Text Conversion:
The S Pen seamlessly converts handwritten notes to editable text in real-time, a feature that feels futuristic and incredibly useful for professionals and students alike.

Camera System

The Galaxy S24 Ultra's 200MP main sensor captures stunningly detailed images, outperforming the iPhone 16 Pro Max’s 48MP primary camera in terms of clarity and zoom capabilities. The Ultra’s 10x optical zoom remains an industry leader, while Apple's telephoto lens struggles to compete. Samsung’s robust Pro Mode also benefits from the S Pen, allowing precise focus adjustments and drawing overlays directly on photos for creative storytelling.

Software and Customization

Samsung’s One UI provides a more customizable experience compared to iOS 17, allowing users to tailor their interface to personal preferences. The S Pen enhances this customization further by enabling gesture controls and shortcuts that streamline navigation. While iOS remains smooth and intuitive, its locked-down ecosystem feels restrictive in comparison.

Battery and Performance

Both devices feature top-tier processors—the Exynos 2400/Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 in the Galaxy S24 Ultra and the A18 Bionic in the iPhone 16 Pro Max—but Samsung has optimized its hardware and software integration to ensure smoother multitasking. The S24 Ultra also has a larger battery capacity, supporting longer usage with faster charging options (45W wired vs. Apple’s 27W).

Verdict

The iPhone 16 Pro Max is a formidable device with excellent build quality and a polished ecosystem, but the Galaxy S24 Ultra goes above and beyond by offering features that empower creativity and productivity. The S Pen alone elevates the Galaxy S24 Ultra to a league of its own, catering to professionals, creatives, and power users who demand more from their smartphones.

For those seeking a versatile, feature-rich device that works as both a productivity tool and an entertainment powerhouse, the Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra is the clear winner.

Update on the S24 Ultra vs S25 Ultra

S24 Ultra
- Box Style shape (Just like the original note series)

- Brightness was tested as ive seen and notice is brighter. (Coating or what not probably causing this but the anti reflection is nearly identical)

- Camera rings are solid and premium (Flush no potential removal)
- 7 years of update (S24U) and was originally advertised as the AI phone already (I use all the AI features Minus the Now brief on the S25 Ultra i had it turned off)
- S-pen location on the S24 Ultra is in a perfect spot for cases (S25 Ultra seems to have it in a odd location where its curved so all the cases have a nasty open cutout in the corner)

S25 Ultra
- Feels like an Iphone which i always envyed iphone users having a flat square display but the samsung design lost its touch reminds me of the redmagic phone (not Note shape)
- Faster CPU but samsung is behind updating a more optimized version for the S25 Ultra
- Nearly only one year extra of uptades vs the S24 U 
- Extra pixels in one camera (I dont see the difference)
- Blue tooth 5.4 vs 5.3 (Dont notice much maybe the 6.0 will be a bigger upgrade.


Conclusion:
Sending my S25 Ultra back and will continue to use the S24 Ultra (I will snag a new one when they come back to the Note roots i have  under 7 years not in a hurry but ill cross my fingers on this one)

I'm a long time Android user and iPhone user for last 2-years. After seeing your video I bought the S24 Ultra. But honestly, it was a mistake and I returned it. Here is why I really dislike this phone:

1. Sharp corners that dig into your hand (I love large phones, like iPhone Max Pros, but not this one). With the heavy weight you feel this phone.

3. The 15+ bloatware apps from Samsung One UI you can't uninstall.
4. Having to sign-up for both Samsung and Google Accounts to use a phone.
4. Honestly I didn't like the photos - too saturated and not as crisp as expected.

While I love the standard apps/home/back buttons that come with Android, I still think iPhone or an Android with rounder corners is better.
